subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should OpenClaw classify and act on plain provider text like `api_error: Internal server error` in cron agent fallback runs: `server_error`, `overloaded`, or cron-local transient only?
rationale: The choice affects shared auth-profile cooldown, same-provider fallback probing, cross-provider rotation, cron retry scheduling, and user-visible failure alerts, and the repository policy treats fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Define policy before repair
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask the agent/provider owner to pick the classification and cooldown semantics before accepting a patch.

options.title: Server-error without shared cooldown
options.body: Treat the plain 500 text as `server_error` for cron retry and observability while keeping it out of shared auth-profile health.

options.title: Overload/provider cooldown
options.body: Treat the plain 500 text as `overloaded` so same-provider profiles are cooled down more aggressively before cross-provider fallback.

recommendation.title: Define policy before repair
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask the agent/provider owner to pick the classification and cooldown semantics before accepting a patch.

likelyOwner.reason: The current main classifier and cron/auth policy files are attributed to recent steipete-authored history, and the decision crosses fallback compatibility boundaries.
